Quick test: sketch i04 survived (user, 2026-10-14, "survived"). Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 4 -> Phoenix-Mesa (its own proposal) and Imperial County (fn 10); Doc 7 -> Northern Wasatch Front (its own proposal) and Imperial County (fn 17). No arithmetic.
- Universe: every area the seven documents tie to contingency measures. Removed because of an approved 179B(b) demonstration: Imperial County (2008 standard; proposed November 1, 2019, final February 27, 2020), Phoenix-Mesa (proposed, Doc 4), Northern Wasatch Front (proposed, Doc 7): in. Suspended under a clean data determination: Washington (Doc 2), Baltimore (Doc 6): out (suspension "for so long as the Area continues to attain", reason clean data). Moderate areas whose attainment determination makes RFP contingency measures unnecessary (Doc 4 fn 15, no area named): out. Coachella Valley's unaddressed contingency measure requirement (Doc 3 fn 47): a mention, out. Sacramento's maintenance-plan contingency provisions (Doc 1): a different requirement, out.
- Necessity: Doc 4 is the only source for Phoenix-Mesa, Doc 7 the only source for the Northern Wasatch Front; Imperial County is in both footnotes (searched "Imperial", "contingency", "179B" in all seven). Without Doc 4 the answer is "Imperial County, Northern Wasatch Front"; without Doc 7, "Imperial County, Phoenix-Mesa". Neither is the gold. Closed-book: Imperial County is a well-known international-emissions area and may be recalled; the 2025 and 2026 proposals are after likely cutoffs, so a recalled list misses at least one member.

Late member: Imperial County appears only in a footnote citation (Doc 4 about 12,900 characters in; Doc 7 about 15,500), never in the body of either proposal.

(b) clean data areas added: five names; rejected by "because of an approved international-emissions demonstration". (c) Imperial County left out because its standard is 2008: the question names no standard. (d) Phoenix-Mesa and the Northern Wasatch Front left out because their demonstrations are only proposed for approval: rejected by "has EPA said" (EPA has said it, in proposals). This is the kind of step the high solver cleared on q01 (Run 1, 2026-10-14, High 3/3); here no name or synonym in the question matches the hidden member. Said to the user before the quick test.

sections.question: Which areas has EPA said need no failure-to-attain contingency measures because of an approved international-emissions demonstration? List alphabetically, or say none.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, section on Moderate-area requirements, and its footnote): EPA reads the Clean Air Act as not requiring EPA-approved contingency measures for failure to attain in an area with an approved section 179B(b) demonstration, that is, a showing that the area would have attained but for emissions from outside the United States. The footnote cites EPA's November 2019 proposal "proposing the same interpretation with respect to Imperial County for the 2008 ozone NAAQS" and its February 2020 action "finalizing the same". So EPA has said this of Imperial County (component c1).
Step 2. Source input (Doc 7, the same section): the proposal for the Northern Wasatch Front states the same rule and carries the same footnote on Imperial County.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 4, Proposed Action): EPA proposes that, once it finalizes its approval of the international-emissions demonstration, the contingency measure requirements "would no longer apply to the Phoenix-Mesa Moderate 2015 ozone nonattainment area" (component c3).
Step 4. Source input (Doc 7, Proposed Action): EPA proposes the same for the Northern Wasatch Front: the contingency measure requirements "would no longer apply to the NWF Moderate 2015 ozone NAA" (component c2).
Step 5. Exclusions and decoys: the clean data determinations proposed for the Washington and Baltimore areas would only suspend the duty to submit contingency measures for as long as each area keeps attaining, and they rest on clean monitoring data, not on international emissions, so neither area qualifies. No other area in the documents is said to need no contingency measures because of an international-emissions demonstration.
Step 6. Final answer, in alphabetical order (Doc 4 and Doc 7): Imperial County, Northern Wasatch Front, Phoenix-Mesa.

Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 4 footnote 10 and Doc 7 footnote 17 record EPA proposing and finalizing the same rule for Imperial County under the 2008 standard.
